meaning.zh:
"还过得去" 或 "普普通通"。

这个短语源于19世纪的农业，在当时 “fair” 表示作物的质量尚可，而 “middling” 表示质量中等。这两个词结合起来，用以描述事物或情况处于中等、普通水平，并没有特别优秀或糟糕。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from 19th-century agriculture, where "fair" indicated crops of decent quality, and "middling" referred to a medium quality. Combined, these words came to describe something that is average or moderate, neither particularly good nor bad.

lines.en: How's your day been? "Fair to middling," I guess.
lines.zh: 你的今天过得怎么样？还过得去吧，我想。

lines.en: The meal was fair to middling, nothing special.
lines.zh: 这顿饭还过得去，没有什么特别的。

lines.en: His performance was fair to middling; not his best work.
lines.zh: 他的表现普普通通，不是他最好的作品。
